data.heroH1: What AI football analysis can see, and what it can miss.

contentBlocks.content: The job has three difficult parts
1. Keep track of what is visible
The system needs to locate the players and relevant areas of the pitch across a moving sequence of frames. Players overlap, leave the frame and become smaller at the far end.
2. Recognise a supported football event
A single image is rarely enough. A pass, tackle, save or goal is a sequence. The model needs enough visual evidence across time to decide whether a supported event may have occurred.
3. Connect the event to the right player or team
Finding a moment is not the same as assigning it correctly. Similar kits, crowded scenes and a blocked view can make player identification difficult.
This is why Pitchside output should be reviewed. AI can reduce the search work without becoming the final authority on every touch.
Why grassroots footage is its own problem
Professional broadcast footage is controlled. Small-sided footage is not.
A phone may be mounted behind a fence. The game may be under floodlights. Substitutes may walk in front of the lens. Five players can enter the same crowded goal area in a second.
Pitchside is developed around real phone-recorded small-sided conditions because those are the conditions the product needs to handle. The current focus is 5-a-side, 6-a-side and 7-a-side football.
Without that evidence, do not publish vague claims about a “huge dataset” or “industry-leading accuracy”.
What the beta is testing
The current beta is testing supported event recognition around goals, assists, saves, passes and tackles, together with the player and match output built from those events.

Exact event availability can change during testing. Product Status is the source of truth.
Physical-load measurements are outside the approved launch promise. Do not describe video analysis as a verified replacement for GPS distance, speed or workload data.
A result is only as good as the view
Better footage gives the model more useful evidence.

Where the human stays involved
Pitchside should not hide uncertainty behind a polished scorecard.

The person reviewing the match needs to know which events were identified, which player was assigned and whether the result can be corrected. The final product should make review easy enough that a wrong assist or missed save can be handled without technical knowledge.
This is one of the clearest differences between responsible AI football analysis software and a page that simply promises automation. The output has to be inspectable.

The Paid plan adds Personal Clips and one recording per week for £4.99 weekly, £12.99 monthly or £99 annually.

tldrPoints: Pitchside analyses pixels and frames from real phone-recorded small-sided football.
The model must track visible players, recognise supported event sequences and assign them correctly.
The beta is testing goals, assists, saves, passes and tackles for 5-a-side, 6-a-side and 7-a-side.
Stable, elevated and unobstructed footage gives the model better evidence.
Human review remains necessary; Pitchside does not promise tactical understanding or GPS workload data.

faqs.question: What is AI football analysis?
faqs.answer: It is the use of computer vision and machine learning to process football footage, identify supported visual events and organise the output into information people can review.
Do not claim tactical understanding unless a specific, tested feature exists. The current launch product is centred on supported match events, stats, highlights, leaderboards and personal output.
faqs.question: Does Pitchside understand tactics?

faqs.answer: No. Recording quality, visibility and current model capability affect the result. Private beta output should be reviewed.
faqs.question: Is every detected event correct?

faqs.answer: Player assignment is part of the developing workflow, but similar kits, distance, obstructions and crowded scenes can cause uncertainty. Describe only the identification method and review flow that are live in the current product.
faqs.question: Does Pitchside identify every player automatically?

faqs.answer: During private beta, upload and processing can currently take up to 45 minutes. The exact time can vary with connection speed, recording length and the current workflow.

data.intro: AI football analysis starts with a recording, not a chatbot. Pitchside processes phone-recorded small-sided football and looks for the visual patterns behind supported players, actions and match events. The aim is to organise a long recording into stats and moments that are easier to review. That does not mean the system understands a match exactly as a player or coach does. It works from pixels, frames and the examples used to develop and test the model.
data.llmDescription: Pitchside AI processes phone-recorded small-sided football and looks for supported players, actions and events across video frames. The capability must locate what is visible, recognise a supported sequence and connect it to the right player or team. The page explains model evidence, recording dependence, human review and private-beta limits without claiming tactical understanding or verified GPS workload data.

data.aeoQuickAnswer: AI football analysis uses computer vision and machine learning to process football footage, identify supported visual events and organise the result for review. Pitchside focuses on phone-recorded 5-a-side, 6-a-side and 7-a-side matches. It can reduce search work, but footage quality, visibility and model limits mean every important event and player assignment still needs review.
